---
title: Embedding apps in Quarto
---

If you write documentation, reports or teaching materials in Quarto, you can embed a Streamlit app directly in the page. This lets people try the app without leaving the document.

There are two main approaches:

- **Using iframes** to embed an app that is already hosted somewhere, such as Streamlit Community Cloud or GitHub Pages (stlite).
- **Using stlite directly** to run an app inside the Quarto page itself, with no separate hosting.

<br>

## Using iframes

An iframe displays another web page inside your page. If your app is already deployed, this is the quickest way to embed it.

<br>

### Streamlit Community Cloud

Wrap this in a raw HTML block (`{=html}`) so Quarto renders the iframe instead of showing it as code.

Add `?embed=true` to the end of a Community Cloud URL to hide some of Streamlit's surrounding interface (such as the menu), so the app fits more cleanly into your page.

::: {.wrap-code}
```{.html}
<iframe width="100%" height="600" src="https://hsma-des-simple.streamlit.app/?embed=true" title="DES app"></iframe>
```
:::

<iframe width="100%" height="600" src="https://hsma-des-simple.streamlit.app/?embed=true" title="DES app"></iframe>

<br>

### stlite

This is an stlite app hosted on GitHub pages. We can embed it in the same way.

::: {.wrap-code}
```{.html}
<iframe width="100%" height="600" src="https://hsma-programme.github.io/hsma7_2g_streamlit_part1/app/singlepage/" title="DES app"></iframe>
```
:::

<iframe width="100%" height="600" src="https://hsma-programme.github.io/hsma7_2g_streamlit_part1/app/singlepage/" title="DES app"></iframe>

<br>

## Directly using stlite

You can also run an stlite app inside the Quarto page, with no separate hosting. This uses the [quarto-stlite extension](https://github.com/whitphx/quarto-stlite) from [Yuichiro Tachibana](https://github.com/whitphx), who created stlite.

1. Install the extension by running the following command in your terminal. This will install the extension in an `_extensions` folder.

```{.bash}
quarto add whitphx/quarto-stlite
```

2. Add the filter to the header of your `.qmd` file, or to `_quarto.yml` to use it across the whole project.

```{.yaml}
filters:
  - whitphx/stlite
```

3. Put your app code in a code block marked `{stlite-python}`.

````{.markdown}
```{stlite-python}
import streamlit as st

st.title("Hello Quarto!")
```
````

```{stlite-python}
import streamlit as st

st.title("Hello Quarto!")
```

<br>

### Limitation 1: Installing packages

Some packages, such as `streamlit` and `pandas`, are available by default. For others, install them in the page with `micropip` before importing them. For example:

```{.python}
import micropip
await micropip.install("folium")

import folium
```

Some imports need to be written differently when using this extension. Plotly and matplotlib don't work with the `import ... as ...` shorthand you'd normally use:

- Use `from plotly import express as px`, not `import plotly.express as px`.
- Use `from matplotlib import pyplot as plt`, not `import matplotlib.pyplot as plt`.

For example, for matplotlib:

```{.python}
import micropip
await micropip.install("matplotlib")

from matplotlib import pyplot as plt
```

<br>

### Limitation 2: Multi-page apps and configuration

You can't create multi-page apps with `{stlite-python}` blocks.

You also can't use a `config.toml` file, so settings such as the theme can't be changed this way.

If you need either of these, host the app separately and embed it with an iframe instead.
